title: Navigating Career Bending Times 2026
author: Rishad Tobaccowala
source: The Future Does Not Fit In The Containers Of The Past (rishad.substack.com), September 19,
summary: Tobaccowala argues that six forces are bending careers at once and that their simultaneity, not any one of them, is what makes this moment different. He lists demographic and generational change, technology beyond just AI, multipolar globalisation, the unbundling of work from jobs and offices, a post-pandemic reset in what people want from work, and the dissolving of industry boundaries. He then draws out the implications for individuals: fifty year careers rather than thirty, recurring returns to training well into one's fifties, work that behaves like a series of gig engagements even inside a single firm, near-universal collaboration with machines, and smaller delayered companies in which many people operate as companies of one. His picture of the resulting organisation is an ecosystem of whales and plankton in which leaders, coaches and learners displace bosses, managers and know-it-alls. The closing advice is practical and blunt: plan careers in phases, build a nameable craft, and do not outsource your own growth to an employer.
points: The argument rests on simultaneity, with six intertwined forces arriving together rather than one disruption at a time.
Tobaccowala predicts fifty year careers and reframes ageism as a prejudice against one's own future self.
He advises companies cutting staff on AI grounds to retrain instead, on the view that AI will commoditise like electricity rather than confer advantage.
He expects an ecosystem of a few very large firms and millions of small ones, with many people operating as companies of one.
Zone of influence and zone of impact replace zone of control and size of kingdom as the measures that matter.
quotes: There are six forces each of which alone might have changed the contours of our career but now they are all occurring at the same time, are intertwined with each other, and are becoming increasingly powerful:
Work is being uncoupled from jobs and from the office. Jobs are a phase that work is going through. Companies and careers will soon be optimized around getting work done versus the filling of jobs.

Extended life spans, limited government pensions, incentives for elder people to stay in the workforce, machine enabled work will have us working for multiple decades versus a 30-year career. Ageism will soon be seen as a prejudice against our future selfs.

Most companies who are cutting people thinking that AI will replace them should actually invest in retraining their people since AI will be like electricity a commodity that every one has versus a competitive advantage.
A job will not be a title, a position and a static role but a constantly changing number of tasks, outcomes and deliverables

The big corner offices, the gauntlet of handlers, receptionists, and other awe-inspiring fear mongering scaffolding of the pre-2020's will all be seen as the crutches of the insecure and the fearful causing most talent to rapidly re-route around such blockages and blockheads.
Do not outsource your career growth to anyone else :Be responsible and control the upgrading of your mental and skill operating system to keep on learning.
